issues.legal_issue: Declaratory relief is available to a claimant with an enforceable interest in property when another person denies or threatens that interest and the declaration serves a practical purpose.
material_facts: The claimant held mortgagee rights relating to the theater and had been assigned a creditor’s decree under which the theater had been attached.
The company denied the claimant’s mortgagee rights and the validity of the compromise decree, and relied on its purported lease in execution proceedings.
The claimant reasonably apprehended that the purported lease would obstruct delivery of possession to an auction purchaser and reduce the price obtainable for the property.
Possession could not be sought when the declaratory suit was filed.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had sufficient legal interest to seek the declarations, the declarations served a practical purpose, and the suit was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 gives statutory recognition to a type of declaratory relief but is not exhaustive of all cases in which a court may grant a declaration; courts may grant declarations independently of that section in appropriate cases. Relief under section 42 is discretionary and depends on the circumstances, and a stranger without an affected legal interest cannot obtain such relief. The Court relied on Veruareddi Ramaraghava Reddy v. Konduru Seshu Reddy; it considered Deokali Koer v. Kedar Nath, Bai Shri Vaktuba Thakore v. Agarsinghji Raisinghji, Kishori Lal v. Beg Raj, and Sheoparsan Singh v. Ramnandan Singh, distinguishing or explaining their relevance.

predicates.declaratory_proceeding: A claimant brings a proceeding seeking a declaration concerning a right or interest.
predicates.claimant_has_enforceable_property_intere: The claimant holds an enforceable legal interest in the property concerned.
predicates.opposing_claim_denies_or_threatens_inter: Another person denies the claimant’s interest or asserts a claim that threatens its enjoyment or enforcement.
predicates.declaration_serves_practical_purpose: The declaration would protect a real practical interest, such as preserving possession or value, that cannot then be adequately protected by seeking further relief.
predicates.declaratory_relief_is_maintainable: The claimant may obtain the requested declaratory relief.

issues.definition: When a claimant in a declaratory proceeding has an enforceable property interest that is denied or threatened, and the declaration serves a practical purpose, the declaratory relief is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A purported transfer that creates new rights in property during pending litigation concerning that property is subject to the doctrine of lis pendens.
material_facts: The company had brought a suit for specific performance concerning an agreement to lease the theater.
While that suit and litigation concerning rights in the theater were pending, a compromise decree was followed by execution of a lease purporting to give the company new rights in the property.
The Court found that the lease purported to create entirely new rights rather than merely enforce an antecedent or pre-existing right.
issues.conclusion: The purported lease was invalid from the outset under the doctrine of lis pendens.
issues.legal_principle: Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act embodies the doctrine of lis pendens. The doctrine applies where litigation relating to property is pending and a party purports to create new rights in that property during the litigation. The Court relied on Jayaram Mudaliar v. Ayyaswami and distinguished the argument based on Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh that the lease merely enforced a pre-existing right.

predicates.property_litigation_pending: A proceeding concerning rights in the property is pending.
predicates.transfer_during_litigation: A party purports to transfer or otherwise deal with the property while that proceeding is pending.
predicates.transfer_creates_new_property_rights: The transaction purports to create new rights in the property rather than merely enforce an existing right.
predicates.transfer_is_bound_by_lis_pendens: The transaction is subject to the rule that dealings during the pending litigation cannot defeat the rights determined in that litigation.

issues.definition: A transaction made during pending property litigation that creates new property rights is subject to the rule governing dealings during pending litigation.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer made while property remains attached in execution of a decree is ineffective under the rule governing transfers of attached property.
material_facts: The theater was attached in execution of a creditor’s decree before the lease was executed.
The Court accepted the concurrent findings that the attachment remained in force when the lease was executed.
The later lease purported to create rights in the attached theater.
issues.conclusion: The lease was also struck by section 64 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Section 64 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies to transfers of property attached in execution and constitutes a special application of the doctrine of lis pendens in the circumstances it specifies.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and property_attached_in_execution and attachment_remained_in_force and transfer_after_attachment

predicates.execution_proceeding: A proceeding to enforce a decree against property is underway.
predicates.property_attached_in_execution: The property has been attached in the course of enforcing a decree.
predicates.attachment_remained_in_force: The attachment continued to exist when the later transaction was made.
predicates.transfer_after_attachment: A party made a transaction purporting to transfer or create rights in the property after its attachment.
predicates.transfer_is_ineffective_under_attachment: The later transaction is ineffective under the rule governing transfers of attached property.

issues.definition: When property attached in an execution proceeding remains attached, a later transaction purporting to create rights in it is ineffective under the attachment rule.
